title: Hindsight
by: Vectorize; MIT licensed. Read from its README and three pages of its docs source in the repo (developer/observations, developer/mental-models, developer/retain). hindsight.vectorize.io and arxiv.org were blocked, so the paper (arXiv 2512.12818) was not read.
summary: A memory server with three operations: retain (store), recall (search) and reflect (reason over memory). Raw facts are kept; in the background they are consolidated into observations, each with its evidence quotes and a proof count, refined rather than overwritten. Above them sit mental models: standing answers to a fixed question, rebuilt when facts in their scope change, and read without any model call.
ideas: Three verbs: retain, recall, reflect, each scoped to a bank (one isolated memory per user, agent or project).
Layers: raw facts (ground truth, never changed), observations (consolidated beliefs with evidence and proof count) and mental models (curated standing answers).
A contradiction does not overwrite: the observation is rewritten to say what was believed before and what is believed now, and the raw facts stay for tracing.
Freshness: when new facts in its scope have not yet been consolidated, an observation or mental model is marked stale and reflect checks it against raw facts.
A mental model keeps its previous versions and the facts and observations it was built from.
Mental models can be refreshed incrementally, changing only what the new facts imply, because a model asked to rewrite a whole page drifts.
Near-duplicate observations are merged above a set similarity (0.97 by default), within one tag scope only.

took.idea: Keep the raw record unchanged and build current views on top that cite it
A stale flag: a view is stale when newer docs in its scope have not been reflected
Standing answers to fixed questions, rebuilt only when their scope changed
Edit only what changed instead of regenerating a page
